Ill or hurt by a fall, the Prophet prayed sitting, signalled those standing behind him to sit, and said the imam is to be followed in Takbir, bowing and rising.
Prayer standing is best, sitting earns half its reward, lying half again; the unable sit or lie on their side, and the aged Prophet recited sitting, then stood to bow.
The Prophet praised Allah on rising for Tahajjud, prayed eleven rak'at with long prostrations, wished Ibn Umar prayed it after his dream of the Fire, and missed it when ill.
When Gabriel did not come for a time and a Quraysh woman said his Satan had left him, revelation came that his Lord had neither forsaken nor hated him.
The Prophet urged the women of his dwellings, and Ali and Fatima, to pray at night, and left loved deeds like the mosque's Ramadan night prayer lest they become compulsory.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, to be a thankful slave, rose at cock's crow, used siwak and stood long; David's prayer and fasting were most beloved to Allah.
The night prayer is two rak'at at a time ended by witr; the Prophet prayed seven to thirteen rak'at, and at night he could be seen praying or sleeping.
Satan's three knots on a sleeper are undone by remembrance, ablution and prayer; in a dream one who slept through prayers was punished, and Satan urinated in an oversleeper's ears.
In every night's last third our Lord comes down to the nearest heaven, asking who will invoke Him, ask of Him or seek His forgiveness, so He may answer.
The Prophet slept early and prayed late in the night, never over eleven rak'at in Ramadan or otherwise, his heart awake as his eyes slept, reciting sitting in old age.
Bilal, whose footsteps the Prophet heard ahead of him in Paradise, said his best deed was praying after every ablution, by day or night.
The Prophet had a prayer rope removed and told people to pray while energetic, do deeds within their capacity, not abandon night prayer, and give body and family their right.
Whoever wakes at night, declares Allah's oneness and asks forgiveness is answered, his prayer after ablution accepted; Ibn Rawaha's verse says the Prophet spends nights away from his bed.
After Ibn Umar's dreams the Prophet wished he prayed Tahajjud, and finding the companions' dreams agree, said to seek the Night of Decree in Ramadan's last ten nights.
The Prophet never missed the two light rak'at before Fajr, praying them after the adhan, then lay on his right side or talked with Aisha until the iqama.
The Prophet taught Istikhara's two rak'at and invocation and two rak'at on entering a mosque, even mid-sermon, and prayed two before and after Zuhr and after Jumua, Maghrib and Isha.
With the Prophet, Zuhr and Asr were prayed together as eight rak'at and Maghrib and Isha as seven, which the narrators thought meant delaying one prayer and advancing the other.
Ibn Umar doubted the Prophet prayed Duha and Aisha never saw it, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at, and he advised Abu Huraira to pray it.
The Prophet kept ten voluntary rak'at around the daily prayers, never missed four before Zuhr and two before Fajr, and allowed prayer before Maghrib without making it a tradition.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at at a spot Itban chose in his house, saying whoever declares Allah's oneness seeking His pleasure is saved from Hell; pray some prayers at home.
Journeys should be made only to three mosques; a prayer in the Prophet's Mosque surpasses a thousand elsewhere but al-Masjid al-Haram, and he went to Quba Mosque every Saturday.
Between the Prophet's house and his pulpit is a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and his pulpit is on his fountain tank.
Four rulings: a woman travels two days only with husband or mahram, no fasting on the two Eids, no prayer after Fajr or Asr, and journeys only to three mosques.
Staying at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet's night prayer; the Prophet twisted his ear, prayed twelve rak'at in twos and one witr, then two light rak'at before Fajr.
Speaking in prayer stopped when 2.238 came down and the tashahhud replaced greetings; men say Subhan Allah and women clap, and Abu Bakr, leading, drew back for the Prophet.
Juraij kept praying through his mother's three calls; she prayed he would see prostitutes' faces, a shepherdess named him her child's father, and the infant named the shepherd.
Levelling the ground once for prostration is allowed, worshippers prostrated on their clothes in scorching heat, and the Prophet touched Aisha's legs stretched before him when he prostrated.
The Prophet said Satan tried to interrupt his prayer and he choked him, but recalling Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom, he did not tie him to a pillar.
Rebuked by a Kharijite, Abu Barza said he saw the Prophet's leniency in battles and would rather keep his struggling animal while praying than let it return to its stable.
In the eclipse prayer the Prophet stepped forward on seeing Paradise and back on seeing Hell, where he saw Amr bin Luhai, who began freeing animals in idols' names.
One praying speaks privately to his Lord, so he spits only to his left; with men's short sheets tied at the neck, women waited to lift heads until men sat.
The Prophet did not return greetings while praying, even on his mount, told people to say Subhan Allah instead of clapping, and hands on hips in prayer were forbidden.
Remembering gold at home during prayer, the Prophet hurried to have it given away; Satan distracts the worshipper until he loses count, which two prostrations make good.
When the Prophet forgot to sit after two rak'at, prayed five, or ended after two, he made two prostrations of forgetfulness; whoever loses count through Satan's distraction does the same.
Praying, the Prophet beckoned Um Salama's maid to wait, Abu Bakr to continue, followers to sit; Aisha nodded to Asma; his two rak'at after Asr replaced two missed after Zuhr.
Whoever dies worshipping none besides Allah enters Paradise, even after adultery and theft, and whoever dies worshipping others besides Him enters the Fire.
A Muslim's rights on Muslims include returning greetings, visiting the sick, following funerals, accepting invitations and answering sneezers; silver vessels, gold rings and silk were forbidden.
Abu Bakr kissed the dead Prophet, weeping, then told the people that whoever worshipped Muhammad, he is dead, but Allah is alive, and recited 3:144.
The Prophet questioned a claim that Allah honoured the dead Uthman bin Maz'un, allowed weeping over a martyr, prayed for An-Najashi, wept announcing three martyrs, and prayed at a grave.
A Muslim whose three children, or even two, die before puberty is granted Paradise and screened from the Fire.
